    #Tutorial 2 (Thrust Equation)

    #Question 1

    Effect of irreversibility:

    • Reduce net work

      Actual work input to compressor is more than an isentropic compressor.
      Actual work output from turbine is less than an isentropic turbine.
      Net work done is thus lower due to irreversibility.

    • Reduce thrust produced

      Less net work done results in smaller change in kinetic energy of propellent.
      Exhaust velocity is thus lower, and the thrust produced will also decrease.

    • Increase fuel consumption rate

      To maintain the same thrust, more fuel is required to increase net work done.
      Higher net work done results in larger change in kinetic energy of propellent.
      From thrust equation, higher exhaust velocity increases thrust produced.

    Critical pressure of nozzle exit,

    Pcr​=528.28 kPa

    Back Pressure Pa​=500 kPa

    Since Pcr​>Pa​ the nozzle is choked.
    Thus, nozzle exit flow velocity is sonic,
    and nozzle exit pressure is equal to Pcr​.

    M7​=1

    #Question 1

    #Part (a)

    State ∞ → State 1t

    q−w=Δh+21​Δ(U2)+gΔz

    0=(h1,t​−h∞​)+21​(U1,t​2−U∞​2)

    wcomp​=h2,t​−h1,t​

    h2,t​=h1,t​+wcomp​

    Work input is negative by convention.

    Assumptions:

    • Adiabatic process
    • ΔU=0
    • Δz=0

    State 2t → State 3t

    q−w=Δh+21​Δ(U2)+gΔz

    qin​=Δh

    qin​=h3,t​−h2,t​

    h3,t​=h2,t​+qin​

    Assumptions:

    • No work done
    • ΔU=0
    • Δz=0

    State 3t → State 4t

    q−w=Δh+21​Δ(U2)+gΔz

    −wturb​=Δh

    −wturb​=h4,t​−h3,t​

    h4,t​=h3,t​−wturb​

    Work output is positive by convention.

    Assumptions:

    • Adiabatic process
    • ΔU=0
    • Δz=0

    State 4t → State e

    q−w=Δh+21​Δ(U2)+gΔz

    0=(he​−h4,t​)+21​(Ue​2−U4,t​2)

    0=(he​−h4,t​)+21​Ue​2

    h4,t​=he​+21​Ue​2

    Assumptions:

    • Adiabatic process
    • No work done
    • Δz=0

    #Part (b)

    From Part (a),

    [1]     h1,t​=h∞​+21​U∞​2

    [2]     h2,t​=h1,t​+wcomp​

    [3]     h3,t​=h2,t​+qin​

    [4]     h4,t​=h3,t​−wturb​

    [5]     h4,t​=he​+21​Ue​2

    From observation,

    h4,t​−h1,t​=(he​+21​Ue​2)−(h∞​+21​U∞​2)

    h4,t​−h1,t​=he,t​−h∞,t​

    Substituting [2] into [3],

    h3,t​=h2,t​+qin​

    h3,t​=h1,t​+wcomp​+qin​

    Substituting the above into [4],

    h4,t​=h3,t​−wturb​

    h4,t​=h1,t​+wcomp​+qin​−wturb​

    h4,t​=h1,t​+qin​

    qin​=h4,t​−h1,t​

    fqHV​=h4,t​−h1,t​

    In an ideal cycle, compressor work is equal to turbine work.

    #Part (c)

    From Part (a),

    [1]     h1,t​=h∞​+21​U∞​2

    [2]     h2,t​=h1,t​+wcomp​

    [3]     h3,t​=h2,t​+qin​

    [4]     h4,t​=h3,t​−wturb​

    [5]     h4,t​=he​+21​Ue​2

    Assumptions for exhaust:

    • Exhaust velocity can at most be M=1 due to converging nozzle
    • Nozzle flow expands to ambient pressure such that Pe​=P∞​

    Ratio of total to static exhaust pressure,

    Pe​Pe,t​​=P4,t​Pe,t​​⋅P3,t​P4,t​​⋅P2,t​P3,t​​⋅P1,t​P2,t​​⋅P∞,t​P1,t​​⋅P∞​P∞,t​​⋅Pe​P∞​​

    Pe​Pe,t​​=1⋅P3,t​P4,t​​⋅1⋅P1,t​P2,t​​⋅1⋅P∞​P∞,t​​⋅1

    Pe​Pe,t​​=P3,t​P4,t​​⋅P1,t​P2,t​​⋅P∞​P∞,t​​

    Pe​Pe,t​​=[T3,t​T4,t​​⋅T1,t​T2,t​​⋅T∞​T∞,t​​]γ−1γ​

    Pe​Pe,t​​=[(1−h3,t​wturb​​)(1+h1,t​wcomp​​)(1+2γ−1​M∞​2)]γ−1γ​

    P4,t​=Pe,t​ as there is no addition of energy in the nozzle.

    P2,t​=P3,t​ as combustion occurs under isobaric condition.

    P∞,t​=P1,t​ as there is no addition of energy in the diffuser.

    Pe​=P∞​ as the exhaust expands to ambient pressure (assumption).

    h1,t​=h∞​+21​U∞​2

    m˙∞​m˙f​​qHV​=(cp​Te​+21​Ue​2)−(cp​T∞​+21​U∞​2)

    1201​(40×106)=1005[240−(−51)]+21​(Ue​2−2002)

    #Part (e)

    h4,t​=h3,t​−wturb​

    h4,t​−h1,t​=qin​+wcomp​−wturb​

    #Tutorial 9 (High-Speed Propulsion Engines)

    #Question 1

    #Part (a)

    #Part (b)

    State ∞→1t

    0=Δh+21​Δ(U2)

    0=(h1​−h∞​)+21​(U1​2−U∞​2)

    h1,t​=h∞​+21​U∞​2

    h1,t​=h∞,t​

    State 1t→2t

    q−w=h2,t​−h1,t​

    wcomp​=h2,t​−h1,t​

    State 2t→3t

    Q˙​in​=(m˙∞​+m˙f​)h3,t​−m˙∞​h2,t​

    m˙∞​Q˙​in​​=(1+f)h3,t​−h2,t​

    State 3t→4t

    q−w=h4,t​−h3,t​

    wturb​=h3,t​−h4,t​

    State 4t→5t

    Q˙​in,AB​=(m˙∞​+m˙f​+m˙f,AB​)h5,t​−(m˙∞​+m˙f​)h4,t​

    m˙∞​Q˙​in,AB​​=(1+f+fAB​)h5,t​−(1+f)h4,t​

    State 5t→e

    0=Δh+21​Δ(U2)

    0=(he​−h5​)+21​(Ue​2−U5​2)

    #Part (c)

    From Part (a),

    h1,t​=h∞,t​

    h2,t​=h1,t​+wcomp​

    h3,t​=h2,t​+m˙∞​Q˙​in​​

    h4,t​=h3,t​−wturb​

    h5,t​=h4,t​+m˙∞​Q˙​in,AB​​

    he,t​=h5,t​

    Combining the equations,

    he,t​=h4,t​+qin,AB​

    he,t​=(h3,t​−wturb​)+m˙∞​Q˙​in,AB​​

    he,t​=(h2,t​+qin​)−wturb​+m˙∞​Q˙​in,AB​​

    he,t​=(h1,t​+wcomp​)−wturb​+m˙∞​Q˙​in​​+m˙∞​Q˙​in,AB​​

    he,t​=h∞,t​+wcomp​−wturb​+m˙∞​Q˙​in​​+m˙∞​Q˙​in,AB​​

    In an ideal engine, wcomp​=wturb​.

    he,t​−h∞,t​=+m˙∞​Q˙​in​​+m˙∞​Q˙​in,AB​​

    he,t​−h∞,t​=m˙∞​m˙f​qHV​​+m˙∞​(m˙f,AB​)qHV​​

    he,t​−h∞,t​=(f+fAB​)qHV​

    #Part (d)

    Compressor (1t→2t)

    Enthalpy at compressor inlet,

    h1,t​=h∞​+21​U∞​2=cp​T∞​+21​U∞​2

    h1,t​=1005(−51+273)+21​(200)2

    h1,t​=243.11 kJ/kg

    Temperature at compressor outlet,

    T1,t​T2,t​​=(P1,t​P2,t​​)γγ−1​

    243110/1005T2,t​​=1.151.40.4​

    T2,t​=251.76 K

    Enthalpy at compressor outlet,

    h2,t​=cp​T2,t​=1005(251.76)=253.01 kJ/kg

    Combustor (2t→3t)

    Enthalpy at combustor outlet,

    Q˙​in​=(m˙∞​+m˙f​)h3,t​−m˙∞​h2,t​

    m˙f​qHV​=(m˙∞​+m˙f​)h3,t​−m˙∞​h2,t​

    1(40×106)=(120+1)h3,t​−120(253014)

    h3,t​=581.5 kJ/kg

    Turbine (3t→4t)

    Enthalpy at turbine outlet,

    h4,t​=cp​T4,t​=1005(301+273)=576.87 kJ/kg

    Case 1 where fAB​=0

    Afterburner (4t→5t)

    Since no additional fuel is added,

    h5,t​=h4,t​=576.87 kJ/kg

    Nozzle (5t→e)

    Nozzle does no work,

    h5,t​=he,t​=he​+21​Ue​2

    Ratio of total to static exhaust pressure,

    Pe​Pe,t​​=P3,t​P4,t​​⋅P1,t​P2,t​​⋅P∞​P∞,t​​

    (Te​Te,t​​)γ−1γ​=(h3,t​h4,t​​)γ−1γ​(h1,t​h2,t​​)γ−1γ​(T∞​T∞​+U∞​2/2cp​​)γ−1γ​

    (Te​576870/1005​)0.41.4​=(581500576870​)0.41.4​(243110253014​)0.41.4​[222222+2(1005)2002​​]0.41.4​

    Te​=510.22 K

    Exhaust velocity,

    he,t​=he​+21​Ue​2

    Ue​=2(h5,t​−he​)​

    Ue​=2[576870−1005(510.22)]​

    Ue​=358.05 m/s

    Case 2 where fAB​=0.5f

    Afterburner (4t→5t)

    Q˙​in,AB​=(m˙∞​+m˙f​+m˙f,AB​)h5,t​−(m˙∞​+m˙f​)h4,t​

    m˙f,AB​qHV​=(m˙∞​+m˙f​+m˙f,AB​)h5,t​−(m˙∞​+m˙f​)h4,t​

    0.5m˙f​qHV​=(m˙∞​+1.5m˙f​)h5,t​−(m˙∞​+m˙f​)h4,t​

    0.5(1)(40×106)=(120+1.5)h5,t​−(120+1)(576870)

    h5,t​=739.11 kJ/kg

    Nozzle (5t→e)

    Nozzle does no work,

    h5,t​=he,t​=he​+21​Ue​2

    Ratio of total to static exhaust pressure,

    Pe​Pe,t​​=P3,t​P4,t​​⋅P1,t​P2,t​​⋅P∞​P∞,t​​

    (Te​Te,t​​)γ−1γ​=(h3,t​h4,t​​)γ−1γ​(h1,t​h2,t​​)γ−1γ​(T∞​T∞​+U∞​2/2cp​​)γ−1γ​

    (Te​739105/1005​)0.41.4​=(581500576870​)0.41.4​(243110253014​)0.41.4​[222222+2(1005)2002​​]0.41.4​

    Te​=653.71 K

    Exhaust velocity,

    he,t​=he​+21​Ue​2

    Ue​=2(h5,t​−he​)​

    Ue​=2[739105−1005(653.71)]​

    Ue​=405.28 m/s

    Case 3 where fAB​=2f

    Afterburner (4t→5t)

    Q˙​in,AB​=(m˙∞​+m˙f​+m˙f,AB​)h5,t​−(m˙∞​+m˙f​)h4,t​

    m˙f,AB​qHV​=(m˙∞​+m˙f​+m˙f,AB​)h5,t​−(m˙∞​+m˙f​)h4,t​

    2m˙f​qHV​=(m˙∞​+3m˙f​)h5,t​−(m˙∞​+m˙f​)h4,t​

    2(1)(40×106)=(120+3)h5,t​−(120+1)(576870)

    h5,t​=1217.9 kJ/kg

    Nozzle (5t→e)

    Nozzle does no work,

    h5,t​=he,t​=he​+21​Ue​2

    Ratio of total to static exhaust pressure,

    Pe​Pe,t​​=P3,t​P4,t​​⋅P1,t​P2,t​​⋅P∞​P∞,t​​

    (Te​Te,t​​)γ−1γ​=(h3,t​h4,t​​)γ−1γ​(h1,t​h2,t​​)γ−1γ​(T∞​T∞​+U∞​2/2cp​​)γ−1γ​

    (Te​1217897/1005​)0.41.4​=(581500576870​)0.41.4​(243110253014​)0.41.4​[222222+2(1005)2002​​]0.41.4​

    Te​=1077.2 K

    Exhaust velocity,

    he,t​=he​+21​Ue​2

    Ue​=2(h5,t​−he​)​

    Ue​=2[1217897−1005(1077.2)]​

    Ue​=520.24 m/s

    Thrust produced for each case,

    F1​=120(358.05−200)=18965.4 N

    F2​=120(405.28−200)=24633.2 N

    F3​=120(520.24−200)=38428.8 N

    #Part (e)

    Thermal efficiency,

    ηth​=m˙f​qHV​21​m˙∞​[(1+f)Ue​2−U∞​2]​

    Change in kinetic energy for each case,

    ΔKE 1​=21​(120)[(1+1201​)358.052−2002]=5.3561 MJ

    ΔKE 2​=21​(120)[(1+1201​+1200.5​)405.282−2002]=7.5783 MJ

    ΔKE 3​=21​(120)[(1+1201​+1202​)520.242−2002]=14.245 MJ

    Thermal efficiency for each case,

    ηth,1​=1(40×106)5.3561×106​=0.1339

    ηth,2​=(1+0.5)(40×106)7.5783×106​=0.1263

    ηth,2​=(1+2)(40×106)14.245×106​=0.11871

    #Question 2

    #Part (a) + Part (b)

    • Increase in entropy across the oblique shock as the shock is not isentropic
    • Decrease in total pressure across the oblique shock such that P2,t​<P1,t​
    • Decrease in total pressure across the combustor (Rayleigh model)
    • Increase in static pressure across the combustor (Rayleigh model)

    #Part (c)

    State ∞ → State 1t

    h1,t​=h∞​+21​U∞​2

    State 1t → State 2t

    h2,t​=h1,t​

    State 2t → State 3t

    m˙f​qHV​=(m˙∞​+m˙f​)h3,t​−m˙∞​h2,t​

    fqHV​=(1+f)h3,t​−h2,t​

    fqHV​=h3,t​−h2,t​

    State 3t → State 4t

    h4,t​=h3,t​

    State 4t → State e

    h4,t​=he​+21​Ue​2

    Combining the above equations,

    fqHV​=h3,t​−h2,t​

    fqHV​=(he​+21​Ue​2)−(h∞​+21​U∞​2)

    fqHV​=he,t​−h∞,t​

    #Part (d)

    Freestream velocity,

    M∞​=γRT∞​​U∞​​

    U∞​=1.51.4(287)(−51+273)​

    U∞​=447.99 m/s

    Stream tube (∞→1)

    Enthalpy at inlet,

    h1,t​=h∞​+21​U∞​2

    h1,t​=cp​T∞​+21​U∞​2

    h1,t​=1005(−51+273)+21​(447.99)2

    h1,t​=323.46 kJ/kg

    Nozzle (4→e)

    Ratio of total to static exhaust pressure,

    Pe​Pe,t​​=P2,t​P3,t​​⋅P1,t​P2,t​​⋅P∞​P1,t​​

    Pe​Pe,t​​=Pthroat​P3,t​​⋅P2,t​Pthroat​​⋅P1,t​P2,t​​⋅P∞​P1,t​​

    Pe​Pe,t​​=Pthroat​P3,t​​⋅P2,t​Pthroat​​⋅P1,t​P2,t​​⋅(T∞​T1,t​​)γ−1γ​

    Pe​Pe,t​​=Pthroat​P3,t​​⋅P2,t​Pthroat​​⋅P1,t​P2,t​​⋅(h∞​h1,t​​)γ−1γ​

    Using “Compressible Aerodynamics Calculator”, oblique
    shock relations for M=1.5 and wave angle β=45.1°,

    P1,t​P2,t​​=0.99972

    From Rayleigh calculator,

    Pthroat​P3,t​​=1.0161

    Pthroat​P2,t​​=1.0783

    Note that flow is sonic at the throat.

    Static exhaust temperature,

    Te​Te,t​​=(Pe​Pe,t​​)γγ−1​

    Te​65.5+273​=[1.07831.0161​⋅0.99972⋅(223110323460​)0.41.4​]1.40.4​

    Te​=237.50 K

    Exhaust velocity,

    Ue​=2cp​(Te,t​−Te​)​

    Ue​=2(1005)(338.5−237.50)​

    Ue​=450.57 m/s

    Thrust of engine,

    F=m˙∞​(Ue​−U∞​)

    F=120(450.57−447.99)

    F=309.16 N

    #Part (e)

    Nozzle (4→e)

    Ratio of total to static exhaust pressure,

    Pe​Pe,t​​=P2,t​P3,t​​⋅P1,t​P2,t​​⋅P∞​P1,t​​⋅Pe​P∞​​

    Pe​Pe,t​​=Pthroat​P3,t​​⋅P2,t​Pthroat​​⋅P1,t​P2,t​​⋅(h∞​h1,t​​)γ−1γ​⋅Pe​P∞​​

    From Part (d),

    P1,t​P2,t​​=0.99972

    Pthroat​P3,t​​=1.0161

    Pthroat​P2,t​​=1.0783

    Static exhaust temperature,

    Te​Te,t​​=(Pe​Pe,t​​)γγ−1​

    Te​65.5+273​=[1.07831.0161​⋅0.99972⋅(223110323460​)0.41.4​⋅0.8P∞​P∞​​]1.40.4​

    Te​=222.83 K

    Exhaust velocity,

    Ue​=2cp​(Te,t​−Te​)​

    Ue​=2(1005)(338.5−222.83)​

    Ue​=482.18 m/s

    Thrust of engine,

    F=m˙∞​(Ue​−U∞​)+(Pe​−P∞​)Ae​

    F=m˙∞​(Ue​−U∞​)+(−0.2P∞​)Ae​

    F=120(482.18−447.99)−0.2(24×103)(0.8)

    F=262.44 N

    #Part (f)

    Freestream velocity,

    M∞​=γRT∞​​U∞​​

    U∞​=1.51.4(287)(−56.5+273)​

    U∞​=442.41 m/s

    Stream tube (∞→1)

    Enthalpy at inlet,

    h1,t​=h∞​+21​U∞​2

    h1,t​=cp​T∞​+21​U∞​2

    h1,t​=1005(−56.5+273)+21​(442.41)2

    h1,t​=315.45 kJ/kg

    Nozzle (4→e)

    Ratio of total to static exhaust pressure,

    Pe​Pe,t​​=P2,t​P3,t​​⋅P1,t​P2,t​​⋅P∞​P1,t​​⋅Pe​P∞​​

    Pe​Pe,t​​=Pthroat​P3,t​​⋅P2,t​Pthroat​​⋅P1,t​P2,t​​⋅(h∞​h1,t​​)γ−1γ​⋅Pe​P∞​​

    From Part (d),

    P1,t​P2,t​​=0.99972

    Pthroat​P2,t​​=1.0783

    From Rayleigh calculator,

    Pthroat​P3,t​​=1.01

    Static exhaust temperature,

    Te​Te,t​​=(Pe​Pe,t​​)γγ−1​

    Te​59.4+273​=[1.07831.01​⋅0.99972⋅(217583315446​)0.41.4​⋅2419​]1.40.4​

    Te​=249.75 K

    Exhaust velocity,

    Ue​=2cp​(Te,t​−Te​)​

    Ue​=2(1005)(332.4−249.75)​

    Ue​=407.59 m/s

    Thrust of engine,
